answers.explanation: Saving the CPU state lets the interrupted program continue exactly where it was.
Polling is simple but slow when there are many devices.
A vectored system goes straight to the right routine, without asking around.
Polling checks devices one by one; a vectored system jumps straight to the right handler.
Each type of interrupt has its own code that knows what to do.
Vectored interrupts go straight through the interrupt vector.
The CPU keeps running the program. It only stops briefly when the transfer-done interrupt arrives.
The interrupted program never knows it was paused.
